title: PROMPTBOX
shortText: Free mystery in a 180 second loop: only what you work out survives each reset
descriptionHtml:
From the same studio: the Games Library holds the CSAF paid games on one page, plus every new one, for $14.99.

PROMPTBOX is a free three-minute time-loop mystery for the browser: five of an opera company, nine rooms backstage, and a casebook that survives every reset.

You are the prompter, hidden in the box at the lip of the stage. The overture runs 180 seconds, the curtain goes up on a corpse, and then it runs again. When the loop resets you keep nothing but what you worked out.

A company on real schedules

Five of them move through the backstage on real schedules. Each has somewhere to be by a given bar, and each one reroutes when a door is bolted, a lamp is out or a prop has gone from where they left it. Leave everything alone and you see the same three minutes. Touch one thing and the night bends around it, so interfering is how the next loop shows you something new.

You see the room you stand in. Next door you hear that somebody is there, but not who. Everywhere else is dark.

Earn your verbs

You begin able only to WATCH. Facts you witness go into the casebook, and the casebook pays for the rest: FOLLOW, then BOLT a door, DOUSE a lamp, PALM what somebody is going to need, and CUE, a line whispered from the box that works only on the right bar.

Stop it, then say whose hand it was

Winning means being in the right place at the right bar to stop the death, with opportunity, motive and method all witnessed. There are three possible culprits, and solving the case deals you a new company with a new secret. Your casebook is saved the moment each fact is recorded: a loop that goes wrong costs you the loop, and closing the tab costs you nothing.

Plays on a phone

Version 1.3 lays the theatre out for the screen it gets: on a tall screen the rooms sit above a message strip and a panel with two tabs, on a wide one they sit beside the panel. Every word on a phone is drawn at 10 css px or larger, every button is at least 24 px, and the whole case can be played by tapping. On a desktop it is the same 960 by 600 board as before: arrow keys to move, letters for verbs, J for the casebook.

Hand-written HTML5, no engine, about 700 KB. Every material, figure and note of the overture is generated by our own tools, and the source ships raw inside the download. Made with AI by this studio: the code, the art and this text.

Paid, from the same studio

  • STRINGLINE, $9.99. Every clue is a line you draw. Drag each crossbow bolt's string back along its flight, round the pillars it glanced off, until every string ends where the archer stood.
  • WITNESS MARK, $5.99. Deduction cases on a real Game Boy cartridge, built on a restorer's term for the trace one part leaves on another. Five cases play free in the browser on its page.
